Best Nintendo Switch Games for Kids & Families (2026)

Roundup · Updated 2026-08-07

The Switch is the most family-friendly console you can buy, but "good for kids" covers a wide range — a game that's perfect for a 10-year-old can frustrate a 4-year-old. Here's our age-by-age shortlist for 2026, with a note on where to buy each cheapest.

Ages 3–5: easy, gentle, no reading required

Look for smart-steering assists and forgiving failure. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is the standout — turn on Smart Steering and even a toddler can stay on track. Animal Crossing: New Horizons is pressure-free: no losing, just a shared island to potter around in.

Mario Kart 8 Deluxe Animal Crossing

Ages 6–8: first real platformers & collectathons

This is the sweet spot for Super Mario Bros. Wonder — bright, playful, and the Elephant form is a hit with younger players. Super Mario Odyssey adds a bigger world to explore, and Pokémon Scarlet & Violet brings creature-collecting they can grow into. The Pokémon version guide helps you pick which edition.

Super Mario Bros. Wonder Super Mario Odyssey Pokémon Scarlet & Violet

Ages 9–12: adventure, competition & creativity

Older kids are ready for The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom and Breath of the Wild (our BOTW worth-it guide explains which to start with), plus Splatoon 3 for friendly online paint battles and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate for couch tournaments.

Tears of the Kingdom Breath of the Wild Super Smash Bros. Ultimate

Get them moving: active & fitness

Ring Fit Adventure wraps exercise in an RPG, and Nintendo Switch Sports is party-paced motion fun. Both are surprise hits with kids who "don't like working out."

Ring Fit Adventure Switch Sports

What to watch: ESRB ratings

Most first-party Nintendo games are E or E10+, but always check the box. Avoid anything rated T (Teen) for younger children unless you've previewed it. Co-op games rated E are the safest group bet for mixed-age families.

Where to buy cheapest

For physical carts, Amazon is usually the lowest mainstream price and the easiest to track — see our full where-to-buy-Switch-games comparison for the full rundown, including used-market savings.

Ages are a guide, not a rule — every child is different. Prices change frequently; verify the current price on the store before purchasing.
